# Independent audit: exact triangle row image and PSD domination

Audited in full: `candidate d61c49578c90db6d`,
Sections 1–6, including the actual geometric reconstruction. Result: PASS.
The positive-octant domination is attained by one actual strict triangle;
the full nonnegative statement correctly uses a **closed** downward hull.

## 1. Actual parameterization

The signed margin matrix has diagonal (a_i>0), negative off-diagonal
entries (-b_{ij}), and column sums zero. Thus the positive principal
cofactors indeed give its right kernel: its adjugate has all rows
proportional to the left null vector ((1,1,1)), so all its columns
coincide. The source reconstruction has positive barycentric coordinates,
and the first two coordinate rows of the matrix yield affinely independent
actual vertices. This proves actual realization, not only formal balance.

The formulas

\[
u_i=(1+d_i-d_{i+1}+d_{i+2})/2,\quad
d_i=u_i+u_{i+1}-1,\quad
f_i=2\sqrt{u_i(1-u_{i+1})}
\]

are mutually consistent. The eight facets of the open (\ell_1) ball
map precisely to (0<u_i<1) and (1<\sum u_i<2).

## 2. Exact forward cubic inequality

Writing (P=\prod u_i), (Q=\prod(1-u_i)), the identities

\[
\sum f_i^2/4=\sum u_i-\sum_{i<j}u_i u_j,
\quad \prod f_i=8\sqrt{PQ},
\quad P+Q=1-\sum u_i+\sum_{i<j}u_i u_j
\]

give the exact deficit (4(\sqrt P-\sqrt Q)^2). Thus every actual
strict vector lies in the PSD region of the matrix with diagonal one and
cyclic off-diagonals (-f_i/2). The determinant and all principal-minor
checks are correct, including nonnegative boundary vectors.

The deduction of each separate Lorentz row is also correct: at fixed
(g=f_j+f_l), use (f_jf_l\le g^2/4) and (f_i<2). Equality requires
both zero cubic deficit and (f_j=f_l).

## 3. Constructive converse

For (f_i>0), the nonnegative symmetric adjacency matrix (B(f)) has a
strictly positive maximizer of its Rayleigh quotient. Taking absolute
values preserves or increases the quotient; a zero coordinate in the
eigenvector propagates along positive edges and would annihilate the
vector. Its largest eigenvalue (\rho>0) is at most one under the PSD
assumption. Radial scaling (f'=f/\rho\) therefore dominates (f).

With (c_i=f'_i/2), the equation (B(f')w=w) gives exactly

\[
u_i=c_iw_{i+1}/w_i,\qquad
1-u_{i+1}=c_iw_i/w_{i+1}.
\]

Both terms in each node equation are positive. Hence (0<u_i<1),
the square-root formula recovers (f'), and the products of the (u_i)
and their complements coincide. The source's expansion proves the strict
sum bounds (1<\sum u_i<2), allowing the actual reconstruction above.
There is no full-cycle-versus-forest gap: this argument uses the connected
three-cycle directly and does not invoke the earlier forest rank count.

An optional completely explicit kernel is available at the positive cubic
boundary. With edges (c_1,c_2,c_3) in cyclic order, take

\[
w=(1-c_2^2,\ c_1+c_2c_3,\ c_3+c_1c_2).
\]

It is positive and is the first adjugate column of (I-B); multiplication
gives ((\det(I-B),0,0)=0). Alternatively the radial factor is the unique
positive solution of

\[
t^2\sum f_i^2+t^3\prod f_i=4.
\]

These formulas are consistent with the Rayleigh construction and make no
additional assertion about general convex bodies.

## 4. Boundary and scope qualification

The closure language is essential at zero coordinates. If (f\ge0) lies
on the cubic boundary and has a zero coordinate, any strictly positive
vector dominating it has strictly larger sum of squares and a positive
product, so cannot lie in the PSD region. For example ((2,0,0)) has no
actual strict-triangle dominator. Such points are nevertheless limits of
dominated points, as the source proves by mixing with the positive-definite
vector ((1/2,1/2,1/2)) and using the compact closed triangle image.

Thus the claimed positive-octant theorem and the closed nonnegative hull
are both exact. Nothing in this audit promotes the cubic inequality to
arbitrary quadrilaterals, general convex bodies, or mixed-integer depth.
